easyocrsharp 3.1.0 — OCR powered by EasyOcrSharp
(EasyOCR's neural models on ONNX Runtime; library 3.1.0).

Usage:
  easyocrsharp <command> [options]

Commands:
  scan    Recognize text in images, PDFs, folders and globs.
  pdf     Write a searchable PDF from a scanned one.
  models  Pull, list and locate the ONNX models (air-gapped deployment).
  info    Versions, execution provider, GPU status and cache location.

Options:
  -h, --help     Show this help. Use '<command> --help' for a command's own options.
  -v, --version  Print the version and exit.

Examples:
  easyocrsharp scan receipt.png
  easyocrsharp scan scans/ -r -l en,de --format json -o out/
  easyocrsharp pdf scan.pdf -o searchable.pdf
  easyocrsharp models pull en,fr

Usage:
  easyocrsharp scan <input...> [options]

Recognize text in images and PDFs. Inputs may be files, folders or globs; results go to stdout unless -o is given. Text goes to stdout and diagnostics to stderr, so the tool pipes cleanly.

Options:
  -l, --lang <codes>          Language codes to recognize, comma-separated (default: en). Repeatable.
  -f, --format <fmt>          Output format: text (default), json, hocr, alto, tsv.
  -o, --output <path>         Write results here: a file for a single document, otherwise a directory. Default: stdout.
      --paragraph             Merge lines into paragraph blocks.
      --line                  Merge boxes into lines (the default).
      --word                  Do not merge: one result per detected box.
      --detail <level>        Sub-line geometry: none (default), words, chars. Gives hOCR/ALTO/TSV true word boxes.
      --allowlist <chars>     Only ever emit these characters (e.g. 0123456789). Sharpens constrained fields.
      --blocklist <chars>     Never emit these characters. Ignored when --allowlist is set.
      --min-confidence <0-1>  Drop recognized lines below this confidence, 0-1 (default: 0, keep all).
      --decoder <name>        CTC decoder: greedy (default), beam, wordbeam.
      --beam-width <n>        Beam width for --decoder beam/wordbeam (default: 5).
      --preprocess <steps>    Comma-separated clean-up: deskew,binarize,denoise,sharpen,orientation,unwarp,rotate. Repeatable.
      --dpi <n>               Rasterization resolution for PDF input, 36-1200 (default: 200).
  -r, --recursive             Descend into sub-directories when an input is a folder or a glob.
  -j, --jobs <n>              Images recognized concurrently (default: half the CPU count).

result.stdout:
Usage:
  easyocrsharp pdf <input.pdf> -o <output.pdf> [options]

OCR a scanned PDF and write a searchable PDF: the same pages, with an invisible text layer that readers can select, copy and full-text index.

Options:
  -o, --output <out.pdf>      Path of the searchable PDF to write (required).
  -l, --lang <codes>          Language codes to recognize, comma-separated (default: en). Repeatable.
      --dpi <n>               Rasterization resolution for PDF input, 36-1200 (default: 200).
      --jpeg-quality <n>      JPEG quality of the embedded page images, 1-100 (default: 75).
      --paragraph             Merge lines into paragraph blocks before building the text layer.
      --line                  Merge boxes into lines (the default).
      --word                  Do not merge: one text-layer entry per detected box.
      --preprocess <steps>    Comma-separated clean-up: deskew,binarize,denoise,sharpen,orientation,unwarp,rotate. Repeatable.
      --allowlist <chars>     Only ever emit these characters (e.g. 0123456789). Sharpens constrained fields.
      --blocklist <chars>     Never emit these characters. Ignored when --allowlist is set.
      --min-confidence <0-1>  Drop recognized lines below this confidence, 0-1 (default: 0, keep all).
      --decoder <name>        CTC decoder: greedy (default), beam, wordbeam.
      --beam-width <n>        Beam width for --decoder beam/wordbeam (default: 5).
      --gpu                   Force the CUDA execution provider (needs the EasyOcrSharp.Gpu package). Default: auto-detect.
      --cpu                   Force CPU execution even when an accelerator is available.
      --cache <dir>           Model cache directory (default: $EASYOCRSHARP_CACHE or the per-user cache).
      --offline               Never download: a model missing from the cache is a hard error (air-gapped hosts).
  -q, --quiet                 Suppress progress and informational output on stderr. Errors are still reported.
  -h, --help                  Show this help text and exit.

The text layer is wri
[truncated]

result.stdout:
Usage:
  easyocrsharp models <pull|list|path> [options]

Manage the ONNX model cache.

Sub-commands:
  pull <languages>  Download the models for these languages into the cache.
  list [languages]  Show what is cached (and what is missing for those languages).
  path              Print the cache directory.

Run 'easyocrsharp models <sub-command> --help' for the options of each.

Usage:
  easyocrsharp info [options]

Report tool and library versions, the resolved ONNX Runtime execution provider, GPU status and the model cache location.

Options:
      --json         Emit the report as JSON for scripts and provisioning checks.
      --gpu          Force the CUDA execution provider (needs the EasyOcrSharp.Gpu package). Default: auto-detect.
      --cpu          Force CPU execution even when an accelerator is available.
      --cache <dir>  Model cache directory (default: $EASYOCRSHARP_CACHE or the per-user cache).
  -h, --help         Show this help text and exit.

Examples:
  easyocrsharp info
  easyocrsharp info --json
